title: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák and Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin regularity
abstract: Endpoint and Serrin regularity criteria for three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes Leray–Hopf solutions: bounded L-infinity-in-time L3 velocity implies L5 integrability, uniqueness, and a smooth representative on positive times including the final time. Includes local endpoint regularity, both Carleman inequalities, spatial unique continuation, and half-space backward uniqueness. Retains the complete ESS production formalization.

informal.ESS.essSmooth: A Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L3 mass is essentially bounded in time belongs to space-time L5, is unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with the same initial datum, and has an almost-everywhere equal smooth representative on all positive times through the final time.
informal.ESS.ladyzhenskayaProdiSerrin: A Leray–Hopf solution satisfying the critical Serrin mixed-norm condition with spatial exponent greater than three, including the L2-in-time L-infinity-in-space endpoint, is unique and has a smooth representative on positive times through the final time.
informal.ESS.serrinCriterion: The endpoint L-infinity-in-time L3 criterion and the Serrin criteria for all spatial exponents greater than three jointly imply uniqueness and existence of a smooth representative up to the final time.
informal.ESS.essLocal: A weak Navier–Stokes solution on the unit cylinder with finite energy, L3/2 pressure, and velocity essentially bounded in time in spatial L3 has an almost-everywhere equal parabolically Holder representative on the closure of the half cylinder.
informal.ESS.essGlobal: A Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L3 mass is essentially bounded in time has no singular point at an interior positive time.
informal.ESS.essL5Unique: A Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L3 mass is essentially bounded in time belongs to space-time L5 and is unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with its initial datum.
informal.ESS.uniqueContinuation: A vector field with explicit weak space-time derivatives obeying a parabolic differential inequality has unique continuation across a spatial boundary under the stated decay and boundary hypotheses.
informal.ESS.backwardUniqueness: A vector field on a three-dimensional half-space satisfying the heat differential inequality, growth bound, and zero initial trace vanishes.
informal.ESS.carlemanGaussian: The Gaussian Carleman inequality bounds weighted field and gradient energies by the weighted heat-operator energy under its support hypotheses.
informal.ESS.carlemanHalfSpace: The half-space Carleman inequality bounds weighted field and gradient energies by the weighted heat-operator energy under its support hypotheses.
